title: Engraved title page: The Last Voyage of Captain John Ross
creator: engraver unnamed
description: The engraved title of Huish's rival account of the Victory expedition, published in 1835 "by an Officer attached to the Expedition", with a vignette captioned "Village of the Natives on Boothia, with the Aurora Borealis".

title: Esquimaux building snow houses
creator: W. Wallis, sculpsit
description: A snow house under construction, the builder cutting and setting blocks from inside while others carry them up - the clearest technical picture of igloo building in the Ross literature.

title: Captain Ross falling in with the Isabella of Hull
creator: W. Eagle, pinxit; W. Watkins, sculpsit
description: The moment on 26 August 1833 when the boats of the abandoned Victory, after four winters and a retreat to Fury Beach, were picked up in Lancaster Sound by the whaler Isabella of Hull - the same ship Ross himself had commanded on his first Arctic voyage in 1818.

title: Commander Ross planting the British standard on the true position of the Magnetic Pole
creator: W. Eagle, pinxit; C. Winter, sculpsit
description: James Clark Ross and his party raising the flag at the North Magnetic Pole on the west coast of Boothia on 1 June 1831, drawn under an arc of aurora. The pole was the one unambiguous scientific prize the Victory expedition brought home.
